fields.text: I am conquered by the Holy Scriptures quoted by me, and my conscience is bound in the word of God: I can not and will not recant any thing, since it is unsafe and dangerous to do any thing against the conscience.
fields.ref: Diet of Worms, 18 April 1521 (tr. Philip Schaff, History of the Christian Church, vol. VII, §55)
fields.insight: The famous "Here I stand, I can do no other" is carved on his monument, but the earliest reports do not contain it; what they do contain is this: a conscience bound to the Word, not to itself. Bind yours to the same anchor and it will hold when the room turns against you.

witness.work: Speech at the Diet of Worms (1521), in Schaff, History of the Christian Church VII.55
witness.quote: I can not and will not recant any thing, since it is unsafe and dangerous

evidence: Owner decision 2026-09-25: trim the disputed 'Here I stand' clause. Text is Schaff's public-domain rendering of the attested portion (CCEL hcc7, §55); Schaff's own 'Note on Luther's sentence' records the dispute (Burkhardt 1869 vs Köstlin 1874).
